newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
Robusta futures in London ended at the day's lows after a rangebound session marked by origin selling and roaster buying on the dips.

There was no reaction to reports Colombian exporters have had to reschedule this month's coffee shipments because of leftist guerrilla attacks and highway blockades across the country. It was said the exporters have not had to declare force majeure on any shipments yet. The ACPC meeting on Friday will keep traders interested, but little of substance is expected. November shed $16 to close at $1,508 a tonne.

In New York after three days of moderate advances, arabica futures ended easier. December lost 75 points to close at 105.70 cents/lb, while March lost 70 points to close at 102.50 cents/lb. The back months lost between 0.60 and 1.65 cents/lb. The market was weaker despite signs of continued unrest in Colombia.

Traders said that Colombian beans continue to find their way to the US market and that the country is shipping its quota of about 1 million bags a month. But signs of mounting trouble in the world's second biggest coffee growing country may have prompted exporters to step up the flow of shipments to get coffee out as fast as possible because of the turmoil.

INDIA - India's coffee exports in 1996 are likely to be a record 2.8 million 60-kg bags despite cancellations of forward contracts by some exporters, industry sources said. The estimate is made on the basis of shipment permits already issued and expected requests for more permits. The previous export record was 2.56 million bags in 1994. Exports in 1995 dropped slightly to 2.486 million bags.

Traders said cancellations have occurred because domestic prices are above world market values. Therefore, traders preferred to sell their beans on the domestic market. It was added that domestic prices are around Rs66 per kg compared to Rs54-57 in the international market.

PORTUGAL - Portugal imported 76,242 bags of coffee in May 1996, 39 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 315,000 bags, 27 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 5.6 per cent to 626,500 bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1996 were Cameroon (24,600 vs 16,900 bags), Ivory Coast (44,300 vs 27,000 bags), Uganda (26,900 vs 33,900 bags) and Brazil (43,900 vs 34,100 bags).
The country exported 40,400 bags of coffee in January/May 1996, 51 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 rose by 41 per cent to 626,500 bags.
